data.title: Simpleads vs Instant Data Scraper: Scored Pipeline vs Free Raw Scraping
data.intro:
Instant Data Scraper is a genuinely useful, completely free Chrome extension — it uses AI to auto-detect tables and lists on whatever page is currently open, and exports to CSV or XLSX with zero setup. For Google Maps specifically, it scrolls automatically but hits Google's own ceiling of roughly 120 results per search, and the raw output typically needs manual cleanup (stray columns, HTML fragments, map coordinates mixed in with business data).
Simpleads' Google Maps Search is a different kind of tool: a guided, filterable workflow that's part of a larger B2B pipeline, with AI scoring and direct CRM export — built for repeatable local prospecting rather than a one-off page scrape.

items.q: Is Simpleads better than Instant Data Scraper for Google Maps?
items.a: For repeatable, scored, CRM-ready local prospecting, yes. For a single free one-off extraction under Google's ~120-result page limit, Instant Data Scraper is a genuinely useful free option.

items.q: Does Instant Data Scraper have a result limit on Google Maps?
items.a: Yes — it's constrained by Google Maps' own page structure, which typically renders around 120 results per search before requiring a new search.

items.q: Does Instant Data Scraper score or filter leads?
items.a: No — it extracts whatever table-like data is visible on the current page with no relevance scoring, title filtering, or ranking.

items.q: Can I export Instant Data Scraper results straight to my CRM?
items.a: No — it exports to CSV or XLSX only. Simpleads supports a direct one-click push to HubSpot and Salesforce alongside CSV/ZIP export.
